pairs.subject: embedded-preview
pairs.evidence: src/app/api/oembed/route.ts:6 This route is an oEmbed provider: it returns JSON holding an iframe snippet of the host's own read-only /embed page for third-party consumers. The host does not run a separately served guest app or keep a message bridge to one, so the subject's precondition is absent. Searching for postMessage, contentWindow, child_process, addEventListener and spawn found nothing in src/app/api/oembed. Across src/, postMessage and contentWindow appear nowhere; the only child_process user is src/v2/ai/cli.ts, the Claude CLI transport, which is not a preview server.

techniques.evidence: src/app/api/oembed/route.ts:24 The route answers with one plain HTTP JSON response. There is no frame message channel, so no correlation ids or pending table are needed.

src/app/api/oembed/route.ts:13 The only origin check is that the url parameter is on the same site (slugFromUrl in src/v2/publish/oembed.ts compares url.origin with the site origin). There are no inbound or outbound frame messages to validate.
src/app/api/oembed/route.ts:4 The route spawns no guest server and manages no process lifecycle; it runs as an ordinary Next.js route.
src/app/api/oembed/route.ts:14 It resolves one published list from the database. It does not discover guest routes from a file tree.
src/app/api/oembed/route.ts:17 The body is a static iframe snippet. No agent is injected into a guest.
src/app/api/oembed/route.ts:15 Only published, read-only lists are served. No guest is changed between views, so there is nothing to checkpoint.

pairs.registryProposal: The golden path's 'When the subject does not apply' list covers the host embedding a guest. It does not name the reverse case: the product publishing itself as an embeddable iframe or oEmbed provider for third-party pages. Adding that case would stop tooling from matching oEmbed or embed contexts to this subject on the token 'embed'.
